items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: When I went to Art Blakey and said, 'Well could I talk to you about Thelonious Monk' it wasn't secondhand information... can tell you about Art Blakey or can tell you about Charlie Parker.

ctx.x: And you’ve had this experience with, fortunately, catching him and Elvin Jones right at the end of their careers. That’s fortunate I guess.

Well yeah, fortunate for me. Also just the way my life worked out, that towards the end of their careers and their lives and so it just signals that there was a kind of changing of the era, with the passing of these musicians. Elvin was a very, very special person, much in the way of Art, very supportive, very loving, of the diaspora in general. Very, I mean in love with jazz music is what I’m saying, just in love with the musicians. I mean obviously when he spoke of John Coltrane there was a reverence, when he…

That’s true. I remember seeing him in a club once and I thought he was fearsome. I mean you say he was a loving person on stage, but I mean he would sweat and you would see his teeth and you said man, this man is —
